# Draft pull request for qnx-ports/build-files (not opened)

**Status:** draft. The recipes are in [`recipes/build-files/ports/`](../../recipes/build-files/ports/), generated by
`scripts/emit_recipes.py`. Nothing has been sent to qnx-ports; the team decides whether to open this PR and with
which recipes.

## Which libraries
qnx-porter's campaign ported 61 libraries. We compared their names, on 12 Nov 2026, with everything in
qnx-ports: the 151 `ports/` and 16 `conan/recipes/` folders of build-files at commit `1964dba`, and the 239
repositories of the organisation ([`results/qnx_ports_names.txt`](../../results/qnx_ports_names.txt)). 21 of the
61 are already there. The comparison with those is in [qnx-ports-comparison.md](../related/qnx-ports-comparison.md).

Of the other 40, 34 built with CMake and have a recipe:

BLAKE3, Micro-CDR, capstone, cglm, cmark, cmocka, flac, flatcc, fmt, json-c, kissfft, libcbor, libccd, libcoap,
libconfig, libdeflate, libogg, libsamplerate, libsrtp, libtommath, mbedtls, miniz, msgpack-c, nanopb, nng,
open62541, opus, paho.mqtt.c, spdlog, tomlplusplus, wolfssl, xxHash, yaml-cpp, yyjson.

Not included:
- libsodium and libmodbus (autotools), tinycbor (plain make) and inih (meson) built, but build-files uses a
  different layout (`build-hooks`) for those build systems. We have not generated that layout yet.
- libgpiod and can-utils do not port. They use Linux-only kernel interfaces (the GPIO character device and
  SocketCAN).

## What has been checked
- Every recipe holds the flags, CMake options, source patch and compat headers from the port that the campaign
  built and tested on a QNX 8.0 x86_64 target. Each recipe's README states that port's test result.
- Built with QNX's recursive make (`make install` with `INSTALL_ROOT_nto` set to a staging folder):
  - `nto-x86_64-o`: all 34 build and install on 13 Nov 2026. The table, with what each installed, is
    [`recipes/BUILD_CHECK.md`](../../recipes/BUILD_CHECK.md).
  - `nto-aarch64-le`: yyjson, wolfssl and flac. The other 31 have not been built for aarch64 through make.
- The first make build of the 31 found five recipe faults, now fixed in `scripts/emit_recipes.py`:
  libccd did not find the `librt` stub (CMake re-rooted its path under the SDP), kissfft installed its CMake files
  to `/cmake` (it sets `CMAKE_INSTALL_LIBDIR` only when not cross-compiling), mbedtls needs its git submodule
  (the README's clone now uses `--recurse-submodules`), nanopb tried to install its host Python generator into the
  build machine's `site-packages`, and flatcc installed nothing (its install rules are off by default).
- Tests on aarch64: the separate aarch64 campaign (QEMU `virt`) reports them in `results/ports.csv`.

## Differences from the hand-made recipes
- Static libraries (`BUILD_SHARED_LIBS ?= OFF`), as tested. Set it to `ON` for shared libraries. cglm, kissfft
  and paho.mqtt.c use their own options for this and install shared libraries; libdeflate installs both.
- Empty `librt.a`, `libdl.a` and `libpthread.a` stubs in the build folder, because QNX keeps those functions in
  libc. Some projects' CMake checks insist on finding the libraries.
- The toolchain file calls the archiver `nto<cpu>-ar` with the trailing `le` removed. The SDP's aarch64
  binutils are `ntoaarch64-ar` and `ntoaarch64-ranlib`, while the compiler variant is `gcc_ntoaarch64le`. A
  static aarch64 build needs this; a shared-only build never runs `ar`.

## PR description (to paste if the team opens it)
> Add 34 CMake ports generated and tested by qnx-porter
>
> These recipes follow the build-files layout (`Makefile`, `common.mk`, `qnx.nto.toolchain.cmake`,
> `nto-x86_64-o/`, `nto-aarch64-le/`). Each was generated from an automatic port to QNX 8.0 that ran the library's
> own test suite on a QNX 8.0 target. Each README states the result and every QNX change with its reason; source
> changes are in `qnx.patch`. None of these libraries had a recipe in build-files or a repository in qnx-ports
> on 12 Nov 2026. Happy to split this into one PR per library, or to drop any you would rather maintain by hand.
